workers-ai-via-gateway.name: Cloudflare Workers AI (via Cloudflare AI Gateway)

build.prompt:
Deliverable discipline. When a prompt or spec lists required output files, place them EXACTLY where specified -- at the cwd root unless the prompt explicitly asks for a subdirectory layout. Do NOT nest deliverables into src/, tests/, lib/, dist/, or any other folder unless explicitly asked. If the prompt says 'a test file you can run with `node --test`', it means a single file at the root, runnable with `node --test <file>` -- not a test directory or a multi-file structure. Match the prompt's named deliverables literally (filename, location, count). Before claiming work complete: re-read the prompt's deliverable list and confirm every named file is present at the named path; run any test command the prompt specifies (e.g. `node --test ./*.test.js`) and confirm exit code 0; for HTML deliverables, confirm the file opens from disk and meets any timing budgets stated in the prompt. When the prompt asks for a README, write it as a markdown document with EXACTLY these top-level headings, in this order:
  ## Usage -- how to open/run the deliverable, step by step
  ## Running the tests -- the exact command, no install step beyond what the runtime ships with
  ## What is implemented -- the subset of the requested feature scope that is in this code
  ## What is NOT implemented -- features intentionally left out and why
  ## Security model -- any sanitizer library used, hand-rolled escaping, allowlist scope, what is and isn't defended against
Each section must have at least 3 sentences of substantive content. A README under 30 lines, or missing any of these sections, is incomplete -- treat it as a failed deliverable and rewrite before claiming the work done. Do not write a one-line README.

For HTML or JS web-app deliverables, the playwright MCP is available -- use its browser tools (`browser_navigate` to load file://, `browser_type` to type into a textarea, `browser_snapshot` to inspect the rendered DOM, `browser_take_screenshot` for visual verification) to actually load and exercise the deliverable in a real browser before declaring complete. Unit tests of a parser function in isolation do NOT verify that the textarea-input-event is wired to the parser correctly -- only end-to-end browser interaction proves that. This is the verification gap that proxy evidence (passing unit tests, valid HTML structure, no console errors at module level) cannot close. For HTML deliverables, treat browser-tool verification as non-negotiable when the playwright MCP is available.

For code symbol lookups (classes, functions, types, methods): prefer the lsp tool when available. For lsp.workspaceSymbol, the filePath argument must be an EXISTING FILE (not a directory) with the language extension matching your search — e.g. any '.cs' file when searching for C# symbols, '.ts' for TypeScript, '.py' for Python. The file's only purpose is to select which LSP server runs the query; the query itself searches the entire workspace. If you don't know a concrete file path, run glob first to find one, then call lsp.workspaceSymbol. Use lsp.goToDefinition / lsp.findReferences / lsp.hover for navigation once you have a starting file:line:character. Fall back to grep only when the lsp tool isn't in your toolset, or for non-symbol text searches (strings, comments, configs).

Superpowers skills are available — invoke them when the work matches: superpowers:brainstorming before designing new features or making non-trivial decisions; superpowers:writing-plans before multi-step changes; superpowers:test-driven-development before implementation; superpowers:systematic-debugging for non-trivial bugs (NOT for symbol lookups — that's lsp); superpowers:verification-before-completion before claiming work is done -- this is non-negotiable on any prompt with named deliverables; superpowers:requesting-code-review and superpowers:receiving-code-review around review points; superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch when wrapping up. Skills self-describe when to use them — check their descriptions for the exact trigger.
